newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: CONSERVATIVES RETAIN GRIP ON LOCAL GOVERNMENT.
newsitem.headline: CONSERVATIVES RETAIN GRIP ON LOCAL GOVERNMENT.

text.p: Lithuania's Homeland Union, or Conservative Party, retained its grip on municipal government with a convincing victory in Sunday's local elections, the election commission said on Monday.
Preliminary results showed the Conservatives garnered 34 percent of the vote compared with 28 percent two years ago, the country's election commissioner Zenonas Vaigauskas told a news conference.

Like the parliamentary elections last fall which brought the Conservatives to power at the national level, Sunday's poll was characterised by voter apathy, with only 39.92 percent of eligible voters casting ballots.
The Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDDP), trounced at the parliamentary level last fall, was a surprise second with 15 percent of the vote, compared with 19.6 percent in 1995.
The Christian Democrats saw their share of the local vote fall to 13 percent from 16 percent two years ago.
The Social Democrats and Centre Union each got nine percent of the vote while the Farmers' Party took six percent.

With firm control at both the national and local levels of government, the Conservatives should be able to pursue their agenda, which includes increasing the pace of privatisation and decentralising the energy sector.
But Vaigauskas said that they would likely have to form a coalition, like they did with the Christian Democrats at the national level.
"With one-third of the vote, the Conservatives will probably need to build a coalition," he said.
Eighteen of the 24 parties in Sunday's race secured seats.
